verb.enter:
In parallel load chunk_offsets[N], cu_seqlens[0:N+1] and
chunk_indices[min(slot,C-1)]
into shared metadata; initialize the Q/K transaction barrier
and publish both at one CTA join. Inactive slots trigger
launch_dependents and return; their a domain is empty.
GroupWidth=2 in Shared mode, otherwise 1; scratch sets are
reused across r.
verb.stage_inputs:
In the sorting worktile, thread 0 initializes N request IDs
and their chunk counts in two local arrays, then insertion
sorts with a strict smaller-count comparison and stores perm
in the workspace tail pad. Other worktiles do no sorting.
No CTA join follows the sort: other warps can issue their
gate copies while thread 0 sorts.
Thread 0 then issues four Q/K TMA boxes. Threads 0..63 issue
predicated g/beta copies for all HeadsPerPrep heads, committing
one group per head. Warps 0..1 wait for their own copy groups
and join warps 4..5 at a 128-thread subset barrier. Warps 4..5
can then compute b/rho without waiting for Q/K; the other
warps acquire the Q/K transaction. The scan halves use
64-thread joins for the cross-half correction. For ratio 8
the local scans, corrections and rho writes are separate
passes across heads; ratios 1/2/3 finish one head at a time.
A CTA join completes this action before Gram work starts.
perm stores need only be globally visible at prep.kernel_done.
verb.signal: Issue the active CTA's launch_dependents trigger after the input join. The grid launch_ready event permits chain dispatch, but none of the coefficient payload is declared ready yet.
verb.gram:
Six warps cover the lower 16x16 tile set. For Shared ratios
2/3, compute Gm and F in one reduction loop sharing K operand
loads; ratio 8 and independent-head preparation run Gram then
query-key loops. Gm is shared BF16, F stays FP32 in registers
until every head in this worktile has published Qd. Entirely
upper tiles are skipped; system construction still loads some
unwritten upper Gm entries but its conditional never selects them.

save_image.meaning: The designated image owner issues one committed shared-to-global bulk copy. Done denotes global completion; KQImage remains unchanged through the complete inverse/head loop and the drain action. Nonowners perform no transfer but retain the action's issue/done events.

verb.skeleton: Initialize inverse diagonal/upper triangle and system/inverse pad columns once for all GroupWidth scratch sets, then join the CTA. Every later group overwrites all strict-lower entries; the skeleton is not reset per group.
verb.system: Build Sys for the next one or two heads using shared Gm and the precomputed per-head decay data, then join the CTA. Scratch from the prior group is reusable only after its publish join.

readout_coeff.meaning: Issue Qd stores directly to global packed tiles from F and b/rho. These stores may remain in flight during the independent column solves; global completion is required at prep.kernel_done, not before solve8.

verb.solve8: Independent columns perform the FP32 substitution in registers, narrow/store valid entries of Ti, then join the CTA.
verb.merge16: Perform the four width-16 merges per head, keeping the rounded Z intermediate in registers, store Ti and join the CTA.
verb.merge32: Perform the two width-32 merges per head using a register Z intermediate, store Ti and join the CTA.
verb.merge64_y: Form the final merge's Y in MergeScratch, then join the CTA to publish it to all merge consumers.
verb.merge64_x: Read Y and the diagonal Ti blocks, store the lower-left Ti block and join the CTA.
verb.publish_group: Copy the packed Ti tiles and b/bc/Ai/Dl to global slots. If another head group follows, a CTA join retires these shared-memory reads before Systems/Inverses/MergeScratch can be reused; the final group omits that extra join. Done covers the shared reads and store issue; global completion is supplied by prep.kernel_done.
verb.drain_image: The issuer waits for the committed image bulk group to finish globally before kernel exit. This does not add a per-head image wait; KQImage has never been overlaid.

verb.setup:
Pitch=40 for VTT<=32 and 72 otherwise;
StageBytes=44032+128*VTT; Partials=2 for VTT<=32, else 1.
Initialize NSTAGE transaction
barriers, release their initialization, then join the CTA.
The entry launch_dependents hint has no in-call successor
in MODE=0. State/output instructions are issued per warp;
only the explicit CTA/warp joins below synchronize members.
verb.warm_metadata:
Before the PDL wait, read cu_seqlens[rank],
cu_seqlens[rank+1], chunk_offsets[rank] and perm[rank], add
them and discard the result. These in-bounds speculative
reads warm index cache lines; the pre-wait perm bytes can
be stale or uninitialized and never determine control,
addresses or numerical outputs. No initial-state or chunk
transfer occurs here.
verb.join_prep: Wait for prep grid completion with the PDL dependency wait. Only metadata warming and resource setup precede this wait; prepared values become usable at done.
verb.resolve_request: Reload n=perm[rank] after the wait, then read the original request bounds and chunk offset. The wait's memory clobber prevents reuse of the speculative value.
verb.prime:
Issue loads for c=0..min(NSTAGE-2,c_n-1).
One issuer arms each stage for
StageBytes, issues the Q/K image bulk copy, one 11264-byte
coefficient/vector copy and one V box.
Done is issue completion, not transfer completion; transfers overlap
state initialization and later computation.
verb.seed: Load the resolved request's initial_state into R after prime, store Rh and join the CTA. Each warp owns one 16-key slice of R across all VTT values for the whole request.
verb.advance:
For chunk c acquire stage c%NSTAGE with parity
floor(c/NSTAGE)%2, then join the CTA. This makes current
input bytes and the previous Rh rebuild readable, and retires
all previous-chunk stage/RhsOutput reads. Only after this
join issue c+NSTAGE-1, if it exists, into (c+NSTAGE-1)%NSTAGE with
the same full-byte expectation and transfer recipe as prime.
That future transfer stays in flight during the following
compute actions. No cp.async wait-group is used by the chain.
verb.project: Read current Qc/Kc and Rh into fragments and accumulate KS/QS. Warps form a 4-by-2 partition of the 64-by-VTT token/value result. At VTT<=32 the two parity accumulators stay separate until rhs consumes KS and finish_chunk consumes QS; QS remains live through the solve. b is present in the transfer but unused.
verb.rhs:
On the full path, form Hrhs in RhsOutput, preload packed Ti
fragments and join the CTA to publish Hrhs. On the VTT=64,
L=1 branch, only row-0 owners form U0, directly store Out
and optional core, and place DU0 in RhsOutput row 0; a CTA
join publishes DU0. The following solve action is a no-op
on this branch; finish_chunk performs its rank-1 update.
verb.solve: On the full path compute U from Ti and Hrhs, separately store Uh and DU, preload Qd and transposed Kc fragments into registers, then join the CTA. This both publishes Uh/DU and retires every Hrhs read before output can overwrite RhsOutput. On a mini chunk this action performs no reads, writes or join, but retains its issue/done events.
verb.finish_chunk:
Each warp follows its own instruction sequence without a CTA
join between readout, state update, output sweep and entry
into final-state staging. On the full path, form valid BF16
Out rows in RhsOutput from QS and Qd/Uh, compute the R update
using preloaded Kc fragments and DU, and rebuild Rh. Then
perform a warp join and sweep only that warp's staged Out
bytes into contiguous 16-byte stores to Out and optional core.
On the mini branch, Out was already written by rhs; read
row-0 Kc after the DU0 join, perform the rank-1 R update and
rebuild Rh, without the full-path readout or sweep.
Nonfinal chunks have no trailing CTA join: the next advance
retires the prior shared reads before stage/RhsOutput reuse.
On the last chunk, if FinalState is requested, each warp
immediately writes its R values to stage 0 at FP32 pitch
VTT+1, then joins the CTA to publish the staged final state.
Full-path overlapping K/Q/V reads were retired by earlier
joins/preloads. In a final mini chunk with (c_n-1)%NSTAGE=0,
stage-0 writes can race other warps' outstanding Kc row-0
reads; the source supplies no read-retirement guarantee.
Keeping this suffix in one action does not order those reads
before other warps' writes. Output global stores may still
be in flight; the source adds no separate store-drain wait.
verb.final_store:
If requested, transpose the staged state to [value,key]
global order. Per thread prefetch one float4 into a register;
in each of VTT/8 rounds load the next float4 before storing
the current one. The last round has no next load and its
subsequently assigned current value is unused. No worktile
follows in this CTA, and no speculative future chunk remains.
Shared/global retirement follows kernel completion; no extra
store-drain operation is present in the source.

verb.project: Compute KS/QS from Kc/Qc and Rh with the math's accumulator split. Warps partition token/value results 4-by-2. KS partials merge at rhs; QS stays live through solve and merges at readout. b is transferred but unused.
verb.rhs: Form Hrhs, preload Ti fragments and join the CTA.
verb.solve: Compute U, separately store Uh and DU, preload Qd and transposed Kc fragments, then join the CTA. This publishes Uh/DU and retires Hrhs reads before output overwrites RhsOutput.
verb.finish_chunk:
Each warp follows its own instruction sequence without a
CTA join between readout, state update, output sweep and
final-state staging. Form valid BF16 Out
rows in RhsOutput, update R from preloaded Kc and DU, rebuild
Rh, then join the warp and sweep only its Out bytes into
contiguous 16-byte Out and optional core stores.
Nonfinal chunks have no trailing CTA join; the next advance
retires shared reads before stage/temporary reuse.
After the last chunk, when FinalRows>0, each warp immediately
writes R to stage 0 at FP32 pitch VTT+1, then joins the CTA.
Earlier operand preloads and joins retired overlapping
stage reads. Global output stores may remain in flight;
there is no separate store-drain wait.
verb.final_store:
When FinalRows>0, transpose staged state to [value,key]
global order. Per thread prefetch one float4; each of VTT/8
rounds loads the next float4 before storing the current one,
with no next load in the last round. Otherwise perform no
reads/writes, retaining issue/done events. No next worktile
or speculative future chunk remains; retirement follows
kernel completion.
